definitions.gloss: polling place; polling station; voting site
definitions.explanation: A designated location where voters go to cast their ballots during an election.

examples.japanese: {投票所|とうひょうじょ}はどこですか。
{朝|あさ}{早|はや}くから{投票所|とうひょうじょ}に{行列|ぎょうれつ}ができていた。
examples.english: There was already a line at the polling place from early morning.

examples.japanese: {最寄|もよ}りの{投票所|とうひょうじょ}は{小学校|しょうがっこう}の{体育館|たいいくかん}に{設置|せっち}されている。
examples.english: The nearest polling place is set up in the elementary school gymnasium.

notes:
Composed of {投票|とうひょう} (voting) + {所|じょ} (place). In Japan, polling places are typically set up in public facilities such as schools, community centers, and public halls.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {投票所|とうひょうじょ}に{行|い}く — to go to the polling place
- {投票所|とうひょうじょ}{入場券|にゅうじょうけん} — polling place entry ticket (sent to registered voters)
- {期日前|きじつまえ}{投票所|とうひょうじょ} — early voting station
- {投票所|とうひょうじょ}の{設置|せっち} — setting up a polling place

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japan, registered voters receive a {投票所|とうひょうじょ}{入場券|にゅうじょうけん} (polling station admission ticket) by mail before an election, which shows their assigned polling place. Voting hours are typically 7:00 AM to 8:00 PM. {期日前|きじつまえ}{投票|とうひょう} (early voting) is also available at designated locations.

RELATED WORDS:
- {投票|とうひょう} — voting
- {投票率|とうひょうりつ} — voter turnout
- {選挙|せんきょ} — election
- {開票所|かいひょうじょ} — ballot-counting site
